clue.text: 8 in varied menu — almost get excited

indicators.note: varied means changed around, so the letters are rearranged
almost removes the final letter of the word for get excited

parts.note: to rouse is to stir up or become excited

explanation.surface: A diner thrilled by a menu offering many different dishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 is MULTIPLE (many). NUME is the rearranged MENU; ROUSE loses its last letter to give ROUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Numerous and multiple both describe a large number, so they are synonyms meaning many.

clue.text: Change 10? Don't change it!

indicators.note: change tells us to alter the order of the letters

parts.note: 10 refers to the across answer meaning a big game, an exam

explanation.surface: An instruction to alter an exam is immediately countermanded.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 is TEST; 'Change' rearranges it. The definition is the proofreader's mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Stet, Latin for let it stand, is the editor's mark telling a printer to ignore a correction.

clue.text: Chooses to get involved, making absurd points

indicators.note: absurd means nonsensical, so the letters are put into a jumbled order

explanation.surface: Someone joins a debate only to make silly remarks.
explanation.definitionFit: To opt in is to elect to take part in a scheme, the reverse of opting out.

clue.text: Ingredient for festive drink in pubs — they have no 9

indicators.note: in tells us the ingredient goes inside the word for pubs

parts.note: bars are pubs
egg goes into eggnog, a Christmas drink

explanation.surface: Christmas drinkers in pubs with no say over what they are served.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 is CHOICE: the proverb says beggars can't be choosers.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb 'beggars can't be choosers' says the needy must take what is offered.

clue.text: More bats coming to second team? That is right

parts.note: a crew is a team, as of rowers
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A cricket side bringing in extra bats for its second team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bats' is the adjective meaning crazy, not cricket bats.
explanation.definitionFit: Bats is slang for mad, and screwy is slang for eccentric, so more bats is more screwy.

clue.text: They remove unwanted bits as well with most of the selections

parts.note: too means as well

indicators.note: most of drops the final letter of the word

parts.note: picks are selections, choices

explanation.surface: Editors who cut extraneous material while making their choices.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads like editing but means removing food from between teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Small sticks used after a meal clear scraps of food from between teeth.

clue.text: Those in cast, otherwise selection of one

definitions.text: Those in cast, otherwise selection of one

parts.words: Those in cast, otherwise selection of one
parts.note: performers in a play; read again, the letters of the word cast offered as quiz options, choose one

explanation.surface: Members of a play's cast, or else one chosen from among them.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a multiple-choice question: the letters in 'cast' are A, C, T, and 'otherwise' (OR) S, of which you select one. Some solvers see ACT + OR + S.
explanation.definitionFit: The cast of a play is the group of performers who take its roles.

clue.text: Many giving learner advice? Cross about it

indicators.note: the cross is placed around the other pieces, as if surrounding them

parts.note: a mule is a cross between a horse and a donkey
L is the learner, as on British L-plates
a tip is a piece of advice

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about whether a learner driver gets many tips, followed by an irritable instruction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like an adjective meaning angry; it is the hybrid animal, MULE, which goes 'about' L and TIP.
explanation.definitionFit: Multiple means numerous or several, a straightforward synonym for many.

clue.text: Select smart response, finally putting nothing in

indicators.note: putting nothing in tells us the zero goes inside the word for smart
in completes the instruction to place the zero within the other piece

parts.note: chic means smart or stylish
O is the figure zero, nothing

indicators.note: finally picks only the last letter of the word response

explanation.surface: Advice on giving a clever reply, perhaps in a quiz, by leaving something out at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Select' is an adjective here, as in 'select wines', not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Choice as an adjective means of fine quality, so a select cut of meat is a prime one.

clue.text: Heartless type shot big game

indicators.note: heartless removes the inner letters of both type and shot, keeping only their ends

explanation.surface: A hunter with no heart shoots a large animal on safari.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' applies to both words: T(yp)E and S(ho)T. 'Big game' suggests hunting but means a Test match, an international cricket match lasting up to five days.
explanation.definitionFit: A Test is the most important international cricket fixture, so a big game in cricketing terms.

clue.text: Resort to guessing just a little bit

indicators.note: to resort is to sort again, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: When stuck, fall back on guessing, only slightly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort' looks like 'turn to as a last option' but reads as re-sort, rearranging TO GUESSING.
explanation.definitionFit: A suggestion of something is a trace or hint of it, such as a suggestion of garlic.

clue.text: In hot spots, supported by fellow not offering 8 9

parts.note: hobs are the heated rings on a cooker
on means resting on, supported by

explanation.surface: Someone in trouble, propped up by a companion who refuses to give a range of options.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 9 is MULTIPLE CHOICE. Thomas Hobson, a Cambridge stable keeper, let hirers take only the horse nearest the door: 'Hobson's choice', no choice at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Hobson's choice is take-it-or-leave-it, so the man it is named after offered no range of options.

clue.text: Oddly dynastic head of newspaper that's also published elsewhere

indicators.note: oddly means in a strange way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the editor, ED, heads a newspaper

explanation.surface: A newspaper boss from a ruling family runs a paper syndicated widely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' looks like odd letters but signals an anagram. 'Newspaper' belongs with 'head of', not the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A syndicated column or comic is sold to many publications and appears in all of them.

clue.text: Again charge one male among rest

indicators.note: among puts the pieces for one and male inside the word for rest

parts.note: repose means rest
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A man is accused again while others look on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charge' is a levy here, as with a tax, not an accusation.
explanation.definitionFit: To reimpose a tax or penalty is to levy it once more after it lapsed.

clue.text: Apart from some enigmas, understood

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Apart from a few puzzles, everything has been grasped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Apart from' reads as one phrase; split it, as 'Apart' is the definition and 'from' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Asunder means into separate pieces, as in torn asunder.

clue.text: Cut up, dug up, subjected to 10

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom upward

parts.note: to axe is to cut
mined means dug out of the ground

explanation.surface: An archaeological find hacked about and excavated, then put through analysis.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 is TEST. 'Cut up' gives AXE reversed, EXA.
explanation.definitionFit: To be examined is to be put through an exam or inspection, that is, tested.

clue.text: Name for rich fabric — could be A, B, C, D, or E

indicators.note: could be says these letters can be rearranged into a different word

parts.words: A, B, C, D, or E

explanation.surface: A multiple-choice question asks for the name of a luxurious cloth, offering five options.
explanation.walkthrough: The options look like the answer choices of a quiz; the letters A B C D OR E themselves are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Brocade is a heavy woven cloth with a raised pattern, often in gold or silver thread.

clue.text: Reason for crack — paper over it in housework?

indicators.note: in places the paper and it inside the word for housework

parts.note: DIY, do-it-yourself, is home maintenance work

indicators.note: in a down clue, over puts the paper above it

parts.note: the Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
taken as written

explanation.surface: Wallpapering over a crack while decorating the house.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid. The crack is a rift between people, not plaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A lack of unity among a group is what causes a split or rift in it.

clue.text: Person who chooses answers inferior to A, B, C, followed by drink

indicators.note: followed by sets the drink after the two letters

parts.words: answers inferior to A, B, C
parts.note: in a five-option test the answers ranked after A, B and C are D and E
cider is a drink made from apples

explanation.surface: A quiz-taker picks the weaker options, then has a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A decider determines the outcome, the one who settles which option is chosen.

clue.text: I am entering E, say, as rough guess

parts.note: E is taken as written

indicators.note: entering tells us the contraction for I am goes inside the word for say

parts.note: to state is to say
I'm is the contraction of I am

explanation.surface: Adding oneself to option E as a best guess in a quiz.
explanation.walkthrough: 'E, say' looks like 'for example E'; instead E stands alone and 'say' gives STATE.
explanation.definitionFit: An estimate is an approximate calculation, a rough guess at a figure.

clue.text: Change to another option, showing intelligence in school

indicators.note: in places the word for intelligence inside the abbreviation for school

parts.note: wit means intelligence, good sense

explanation.surface: A clever pupil changes course at school.
explanation.definitionFit: To switch is to swap from one thing to a different one.

clue.text: Evaluate dunces, repeating one part for the fourth time

parts.note: asses are fools, dunces

parts.words: repeating one part for the fourth time
parts.note: the word for dunces contains three of one letter; repeating it gives that letter a fourth time

explanation.surface: A teacher grading slow pupils by making them repeat a section yet again.
explanation.walkthrough: ASSES already has three S's; one more S makes four.
explanation.definitionFit: To assess is to judge or measure the worth of something, which is to evaluate it.

clue.text: We agree about pressure on European ancestors of ours?

indicators.note: about puts the word of agreement around the other two pieces

parts.note: amen means so be it, an expression of agreement
P is the symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: People consenting to European pressure on their forebears.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that apemen as human ancestors is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Apelike primates are popularly thought of as the forerunners of humankind.

clue.text: Put in A, B, C, D, or E, say? I'm naive — it's wrong

definitions.text: Put in A, B, C, D, or E, say?

indicators.note: wrong says these letters are set out in the wrong order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A confused quiz-taker confesses naivety about which option to choose.
explanation.walkthrough: A, B, C, D and E look like quiz options but are vitamins here.
explanation.definitionFit: To vitaminise food is to enrich it by adding vitamins such as A, C or E.

clue.text: Missing some obvious answers

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A quiz sheet lacking a few of the easy answers.
explanation.definitionFit: Sans is French for without, used in English to mean lacking.

clue.text: Swing killed a lot in US? All of the above

definitions.meaning: American informal for a large number

explanation.surface: A multiple choice question with three options, the last being 'All of the above'.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions; 'All of the above' says each fits, a quiz option.
explanation.definitionFit: Slew means to swivel round, was slain's past tense, and in America a great many.

clue.text: Agree possible sequence of answers for 8, 9, 10 with five options

definitions.text: possible sequence of answers for 8, 9, 10 with five options
definitions.meaning: a multiple choice test labels its five options A to E, so six picks could run ...

explanation.surface: Accept one string of answers to a five-option quiz.
explanation.walkthrough: 8, 9, 10 is MULTIPLE CHOICE TEST; its options are A to E, and these six picks spell the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To accede to a request is to consent or assent to it.

clue.text: A, B, C etc, as periodically arranged? He and I are with them

definitions.meaning: the ABC of a subject means its basics, its rudiments

definitions.text: as periodically arranged? He and I are with them
definitions.meaning: helium (He) and iodine (I) are among the chemical substances set out in the periodic table

explanation.surface: Letters of the alphabet, and a cryptic hint that he and I belong with them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He and I' look like pronouns; they are the symbols for helium and iodine. B and C (boron, carbon) are elements too, and A was once argon's symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: The basics of a subject are its rudiments; chemically, substances like helium are fundamental substances in the periodic table.
